title: Identify Target Component and Placement for New Buttons
description: Determine the appropriate location within the UI to add the new feature buttons (e.g., 'AI Search', 'AI Image Generation'), ensuring alignment with the existing design and user flow.
details: Review the structure of 'app/page.tsx' and 'app/dashboard/page.tsx' to decide where the new buttons will provide the best user experience. Consider placing them near existing feature controls or in a sidebar for discoverability. Ensure the placement does not disrupt mobile responsiveness or accessibility.
test_strategy: Visually inspect the UI in development mode on both desktop and mobile breakpoints to confirm the chosen location is logical, accessible, and does not break the layout.

title: Implement New Buttons Using shadcn/ui Components
description: Add 'AI Search' and 'AI Image Generation' buttons using the shadcn/ui Button component, ensuring visual consistency and accessibility.
details: Import the Button component from '@/components/ui/button'. For each new feature, instantiate a Button with descriptive text (e.g., 'AI Search', 'AI Image Generation'). If icons are desired, import from 'lucide-react' and include them within the Button. Apply the appropriate variant (e.g., 'default', 'outline') to match the existing UI. Use aria-labels for icon-only buttons. Place the buttons in the location determined in Task 1.
test_strategy: Render the page and verify that the new buttons appear with correct text, icons, and styles. Use React Testing Library to assert their presence and accessibility attributes.

title: Add State Management and Event Handlers for Buttons
description: Wire up basic state management and placeholder onClick handlers for the new buttons to prepare for future feature integration.
details: Use React's useState hook to manage the active state if the buttons are part of a toggle group. For each button, add an onClick handler (e.g., handleNavigateToSearch, handleCreateNewImage) that currently logs an action or sets local state. Ensure handlers are named semantically for clarity and future extensibility.
test_strategy: Use React Testing Library to simulate button clicks and verify that the correct handler is called (e.g., by checking console output or state changes).

title: Ensure Responsive Design and Accessibility
description: Verify that the new buttons maintain UI responsiveness and meet accessibility standards across devices and screen readers.
details: Test the UI on various screen sizes to ensure the new buttons do not break the layout. Use Tailwind CSS utilities as needed for spacing and alignment. Confirm that all buttons have accessible labels and are keyboard navigable. Use ARIA attributes where appropriate.
test_strategy: Manually test on desktop and mobile browsers. Use accessibility tools (e.g., axe, Lighthouse) to check for issues. Write a test to ensure buttons are reachable via keyboard navigation.

title: Write Component-Level Tests for New Buttons
description: Create Jest and React Testing Library tests to verify rendering, styling, and interaction of the new buttons.
details: Write tests that assert: (1) Buttons render with correct text and icons; (2) Correct styles/variants are applied; (3) onClick handlers are triggered; (4) Accessibility attributes are present. Place tests alongside the component or in a dedicated __tests__ directory as per project convention.
test_strategy: Run the test suite and ensure all tests pass. Use coverage tools to confirm all new logic is tested. Address any visual regressions if using snapshot or visual regression testing.
